title: v1-chat-compat-param-normalizer-role-coercion-and-structured-toolcall-stability
author: Ethan Kwan
release_notes: Normalize /v1/chat params (roles/stop/logprobs), coerce numeric stop inputs to canonical arrays, and harden streaming toolcall framing for mixed structured/plain text outputs. No breaking changes expected.
description:
Context: Customers using the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer hit a few edge-cases when mixing older client payloads with newer structured tool/function calling. In particular: 1) numeric/boolean stop values emitted by upstream proxies were being passed through and causing unexpected behavior; 2) role aliases (assistant/system/user) were not consistently normalized which hurt our role-based delta compression and safety heuristics; 3) streaming toolcall fragments occasionally produced invalid JSON fragments when interleaved with plain text deltas.

Motivation: Provide a conservative, backwards-compatible layer that coerces and normalizes incoming /v1/chat parameters to our canonical v2 internal shape, while fixing a handful of regressions observed in customer telemetry and SRE incident reports (ENG-3742). This reduces operator confusion and prevents toolcall stream deserialization errors without changing surface-level API semantics for well-formed clients.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a param coercion module for /v1/chat that:
  - coerces non-string stop entries (numbers/booleans) into their string equivalents and wraps single stops into arrays
  - canonicalizes role names and role-aliases (e.g. 'system_message' -> 'system') and dedupes contiguous role tokens
  - preserves original raw param metadata on the request context for telemetry/debugging
- Improves streaming framer to support atomic toolcall envelopes when tool outputs are emitted interleaved with plain text, reducing malformed JSON fragments in the stream
- Normalizes logprob packaging under /v1 compatibility so clients get stable shape regardless of model variant
- Adds extensive unit and integration tests, and small SDK compatibility shim in the Python SDK to demonstrate safe coercion behavior

Checklist:
- [x] Param coercion logic implemented and tested
- [x] Streaming framer extended and regression tests added
- [x] SDK example updated
- [x] Docs snippet updated (compat notes)
- [x] Metrics added for coercion hits and stream-framer errors

Commits (high-level):
- feat(api): add param_coercer for /v1/chat compatibility
- fix(stream): atomic toolcall envelope framing in stream framer
- perf(runtime): avoid extra allocations when normalizing role arrays
- test: add interleaved streaming integration test and unit tests for coercion
- docs: update openai_v1_chat compatibility notes and examples

Files/areas changed (high level):
- lib/api/v1/param_coercer.py — new module; handles type coercion and normalization
- runtime/stream/framer.go — extend framer to emit atomic toolcall JSON envelope boundaries
- runtime/stream/framer_test.go — new regression tests covering interleaving scenarios
- sdk/python/redwood_openai_compat.py — small shim showing client expectations
- docs/reference/openai_v1_chat.md — compatibility notes and examples
- telemetry/metrics_defs.yaml — counters: v1_param_coercions, stream_framer_malformed
- tools/observability/dashboards/compatibility.json — dashboard tile for coercion rate

Review conversation (selected):
- Priya Nair: "Can we ensure coercion is only applied to the /v1 compatibility path and that we preserve raw payload for audit?"  
  - Author: "Yes — coercion lives in lib/api/v1 and we attach original_payload to the request context; added tests to validate roundtrip for raw payload visibility."  
- Lucas Moreno: "Edge-case: what if a client intentionally sends numeric stop tokens to trigger model behavior? Are we changing semantics?"  
  - Author: "We coerce numbers to strings (the safest mapping) and emit a 'coercion_applied' metric. There is also an opt-out header X-Redwood-Allow-Raw-V1 that keeps behavior strict for advanced users — documented in the compatibility notes."  
- Jin Park: "Framer changes look safe but please add a benchmark — we can't add pathological allocations to the hot path."  
  - Author: "Added a micro-benchmark and used a pooled buffer path when atomic envelopes are detected; results included in the PR comments."  

CI and validation:
- CI run #1 (linux/unit): fail — flakey test in framer_test.go (race on buffer reuse)
- Fix: add locking around buffer pool and rerun
- CI run #2: pass all (unit/integration/lint)
- Staging deployment: manual smoke tests w/ legacy clients and new clients passed

Migration notes for operators:
- No migration required for most customers. The coercion is opt-out via header if strict behavior is required. Operators can monitor telemetry (v1_param_coercions) for how often coercion runs and decide if additional communication to clients is needed.

Risk and mitigation:
- Risk: subtle behavior change for rare clients that relied on non-string stop semantics. Mitigation: opt-out header, metric visibility, and a two-week feature flag window in production before fully unflagging.

Merge outcome: Squashed and merged into main. Merged by Priya Nair after green CI and 2 approvals.
